steps.message:
ModelGate is the static scanner our model registry runs on every uploaded artifact before accepting it. It lives in `/app/modelgate/` and the registry invokes it once per artifact as `python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output /tmp/report.json /path/to/artifact`, reading the JSON report described in `/app/docs/report-schema.md`. The red team has shown that artifacts which run code when loaded get past it, and that it also flags some legitimate models. Harden the scanner so that its verdict matches the registry policy in `/app/docs/threat-model.md` for every artifact that policy covers: an artifact is `malicious` when loading it with its format's standard loader, or invoking a function it exports, would execute attacker-controlled code, start a process, access files outside the artifact, or open a network connection, and `clean` otherwise. A missed malicious artifact and a flagged legitimate one are equally wrong.

The registry grades the scanner on its own held-out corpus, built to the threat model, not on the examples in `/app/samples/`. Those examples, their labels in `/app/samples/labels.json` and the harness `/app/evaluate.py` show the formats, containers and report format, but they do not cover every technique the threat model describes. Only `/app/modelgate/` is deployed, so everything the scanner needs must live there, and the command line and report schema above must keep working unchanged. Scanning must never cause any behaviour of an artifact to run: the registry runs the scanner in an isolated sandbox and treats any process it starts, any network connection it opens and any file it writes other than its report as a failed scan. The registry scans its held-out corpus of roughly 560 artifacts in one pass, invoking the scanner once per artifact; the whole pass must finish within 900 seconds and no single artifact may take more than 60 seconds, using only the Python packages already installed in this environment.

You have 28800 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.
I'll start by exploring the environment to understand the scanner, docs, and samples.

results.content:
# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious

This is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the
only definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it
but do not enumerate it.

## 1. Policy

An artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's
standard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of
the following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:

- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or
  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that
  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a
  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another
  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what
  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a
  finding.
- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.
- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the
  artifact itself.
- **(D) network**: open a network connection.

Every other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false
negative are equally wrong.

Capabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a
dictionary value `"subprocess"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant
tensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached
through a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a
`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the
first `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a
finding.

Standard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:

| Format | Loader |
|---|---|
| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |
| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |
| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |
| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |
| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |

## 2. Formats and containers in scope

| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |
| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |
| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | `torch.load` unpickles all five streams in order; the object pickle is the fourth |
| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |
| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |
| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |
| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |

Out of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,
TorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,
Keras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual
datasets, archives with 64-bit sizes or zip64 extra fields.

## 3. Pickle semantics the policy follows

These are the facts of CPython's unpickler; the policy is defined in terms of
what the loader would actually do.

- `REDUCE` calls the callable with the arguments (a tuple: `pickle.load`'s C
  unpickler raises on anything else before calling); on a class that runs
  `__new__` and `__init__`. `INST` and `OBJ` with arguments construct fully.
  `BUILD` calls `__setstate__` on the object (for `functools.partial` that
  retargets the partial) or, when there is none, writes the state into the
  object's `__dict__`, which on a module rebinds its attributes for every
  later `GLOBAL`. These are the ways a capability executes. A dotted name in
  `GLOBAL`/`STACK_GLOBAL` (`Bdb.run`, `os.system` under module `shutil`)
  resolves attribute by attribute at protocol 4 and above and fails the load
  below that.
- `NEWOBJ` and `NEWOBJ_EX` call `__new__` only; argument-less `INST`/`OBJ`
  call `__new__` only when the target is a class, and call any other callable
  (a `functools.partial`, a function) with no arguments. `PERSID`/`BINPERSID`
  are resolved by the loader's own storage mechanism (`torch.load`) and
  execute nothing; plain `pickle.load` has no persistent-id handler and stops
  there. Importing a module executes no capability.
- A global that is only stored as data (placed in a container, bound as an
  attribute, memoised and never called) is not a finding, whatever its name.
  A global becomes a finding when the capability it carries is executed, no
  matter how it reached the executing opcode: directly, through the memo
  (`GET`, `BINGET`, `LONG_BINGET`), through `builtins.getattr`,
  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller`, `functools.partial`,
  `builtins.__import__` or `importlib.import_module`, or in a later stream of
  the same file. Those are examples, not a list: any route by which the
  loader ends up calling the capability counts, among them a module reached
  through `sys.modules`, `vars()` or another module's attribute
  (`shutil.os` is `os`), a name resolved by
  `pkgutil.resolve_name`, a function handed back by a wrapper such as
  `functools.lru_cache` or `copy.copy`, and a callable passed to something
  that calls it (`map`, `filter` or `itertools.starmap` once something
  consumes the iterator; `sorted`, `min` or `max` through `key`;
  `functools.reduce`; `operator.call`; a thread or executor started with
  it). A lazy iterator that is built and never consumed executes nothing.
- A nested loader reads what its own loader reads: `pickle.loads` and
  `pickle.load` read one pickle and ignore trailing bytes, `torch.load` on a
  legacy checkpoint unpickles all five streams, and embedded data that the
  pickle first decodes or assembles (`base64`, `zlib`, `bytes.fromhex`,
  concatenation, a `bytearray` literal) is judged after that step.
- Module aliases are the same module: `posix` and `nt` are `os`, `_pickle` is
  `pickle`, `_io` is `io`, and every Python 2 name the unpickler maps back
  with `fix_imports` (the `_compat_pickle` tables): `__builtin__` is
  `builtins`, `copy_reg` is `copyreg`, `commands` is `subprocess`, `urllib2`
  is `urllib.request`, `httplib` is `http.client`, and so on. Pickles written
  below protocol 3 carry those Python 2 names.

Representative capability-bearing callables (a seed list, not the policy;
anything with the same capability counts):

- (A) `builtins.eval`, `builtins.exec`, `builtins.compile`, `marshal.loads`
  with `types.FunctionType`,
  `runpy.run_path`, `runpy._run_code`, `timeit.timeit`,
  `code.InteractiveInterpreter.runsource`, `bdb.Bdb.run`, `pdb.run`,
  `numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring`, `logging.config.dictConfig`;
  nested loaders `pickle.loads`, `_pickle.loads`, `torch.load`,
  `torch.storage._load_from_bytes`, `numpy.load`,
  `numpy.lib.format.read_array`, `joblib.load`, `pandas.read_pickle`.
  `builtins.__import__`, `importlib.import_module`, `builtins.getattr`,
  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller` and `functools.partial`
  carry no capability of their own; they are the ways a capability-bearing
  callable is reached, and the call that reaches it is the finding.
- (B) `os.system`, `os.popen`, `os.execv`, `os.execvp`, `os.execve`,
  `os.spawnl`, `os.spawnv`, `os.posix_spawn`, `subprocess.Popen`,
  `subprocess.call`, `subprocess.run`, `subprocess.check_call`,
  `subprocess.check_output`, `pty.spawn`, `pydoc.pipepager`.
- (C) `builtins.open`, `io.open`, `os.remove`, `os.unlink`, `os.rename`,
  `os.replace`, `os.mkdir`, `os.makedirs`, `os.rmdir`, `shutil.copy`,
  `shutil.copyfile`, `shutil.move`, `shutil.rmtree`, `pathlib.Path.write_text`,
  `pathlib.Path.write_bytes`, `pathlib.Path.unlink`; a nested loader given a
  path instead of embedded data reads that path.
- (D) `socket.create_connection`, `socket.socket.connect`,
  `urllib.request.urlopen`, `http.client.HTTPConnection.connect` and
  `.request`, `ftplib.FTP.connect` and `ftplib.FTP(host)`,
  `smtplib.SMTP(host)`, `ssl.get_server_certificate`, `webbrowser.open`. The
  capability is in the call that connects: constructing a client object
  without a host (`socket.socket()`, `http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)`,
  `ftplib.FTP()`, `xmlrpc.client.ServerProxy(uri)`) opens nothing.

## 4. TensorFlow op table (closed)

For TensorFlow graphs the table is the policy: an op listed here has the
capability listed, and an op not listed has none, wherever it appears.

| Capability | Ops |
|---|---|
| (A) code execution | `PyFunc` `PyFuncStateless` `EagerPyFunc` |

# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious

This is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the
only definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it
but do not enumerate it.

## 1. Policy

An artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's
standard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of
the following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:

- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or
  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that
  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a
  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another
  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what
  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a
  finding.
- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.
- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the
  artifact itself.
- **(D) network**: open a network connection.

Every other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false
negative are equally wrong.

Capabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a
dictionary value `"subprocess"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant
tensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached

`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the
first `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a
finding.

Standard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:

| Format | Loader |
|---|---|
| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |
| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |
| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |
| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |
| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |

| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |
| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |
| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | `torch.load` unpickles all five streams in order; the object pickle is the fourth |
| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |
| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |

| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |

Out of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,

datasets, archives with 64-bit sizes or zip64 extra fields.

# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious

This is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the
only definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it
but do not enumerate it.

## 1. Policy

An artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's
standard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of
the following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:

- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or
  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that
  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a
  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another
  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what
  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a
  finding.
- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.
- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the
  artifact itself.
- **(D) network**: open a network connection.

Every other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false
negative are equally wrong.

Capabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a
dictionary value `"subprocess"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant
tensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached
through a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a
`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the
first `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a
finding.

Standard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:

| Format | Loader |
|---|---|
| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |
| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |
| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |
| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |
| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |

## 2. Formats and containers in scope

| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |
| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |
| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | `torch.load` unpickles all five streams in order; the object pickle is the fourth |
| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |
| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |
| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |
| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |
| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |

Out of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,
TorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,
Keras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ModelGate command line.

    python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path> [<path> ...]

Writes one JSON report (see /app/docs/report-schema.md) and exits 0 once it
is written; exits 2 on a usage error.  ``-I`` keeps the script directory off
sys.path, so the package directory's parent is added explicitly below.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from modelgate import __version__  # noqa: E402
from modelgate import dispatch  # noqa: E402
from modelgate.report import Finding, Result, to_json  # noqa: E402


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="modelgate", description="static scanner for model artifacts")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"modelgate {__version__}")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    scan = sub.add_parser("scan", help="scan one or more artifacts")
    scan.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="where to write the JSON report")
    scan.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="artifact files, or SavedModel directories")
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        return 2 if exc.code else 0

    results = []
    for path in args.paths:
        try:
            results.append(dispatch.scan_path(path))
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a crash must still yield a verdict
            results.append(Result(path, [Finding("unsupported", path, f"scanner error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")]))
    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(to_json(results))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
"""Choose a scanner by artifact type and build the result."""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import os
import zipfile

from modelgate import keras_scan, pickle_scan, savedmodel_scan
from modelgate.report import Result

PICKLE_EXTS = (".pkl", ".pickle", ".joblib")
TORCH_EXTS = (".pt", ".pth", ".ckpt", ".bin")  # .bin: a torch checkpoint or a plain pickle
H5_EXTS = (".h5", ".hdf5")


def scan_path(path: str) -> Result:
    name = os.path.basename(path.rstrip("/"))
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        return Result(path, savedmodel_scan.scan_saved_model_dir(path))
    ext = os.path.splitext(name)[1].lower()
    if ext in PICKLE_EXTS:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            return Result(path, pickle_scan.scan_pickle(fh.read(), name))
    if ext in TORCH_EXTS:
        return Result(path, _scan_torch(path, name))
    if ext in H5_EXTS:
        return Result(path, keras_scan.scan_h5(path, name))
    # .npy, .npz, .keras and compressed archives are not model formats the
    # scanner understands; nothing to report for them
    return Result(path, [])


def _scan_torch(path: str, name: str):
    """A torch checkpoint is a zip whose data.pkl holds the object graph."""
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        data = fh.read()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the ModelGate scanner over /app/samples the way the registry does and
compare its verdicts with /app/samples/labels.json.

Usage: python3 /app/evaluate.py [--samples DIR] [--scanner /app/modelgate/cli.py]

The scanner is invoked as a separate process per artifact, with the same
command line the registry uses, so this script never imports the scanner.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

KINDS = {"code-execution", "process", "file-access", "network", "unsupported"}


def run_scanner(cli, artifact, timeout=60):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        report = os.path.join(tmp, "report.json")
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-I", cli, "scan", "--output", report, artifact]
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, "timeout", time.monotonic() - started
        seconds = time.monotonic() - started
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"exit {proc.returncode}: {proc.stderr.strip()[-200:]}", seconds
        try:
            with open(report, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                doc = json.load(f)

"""Pickle stream scanning.

Walks the opcodes of a pickle with ``pickletools.genops`` and reports any
global reference on the blocklist.  ``GLOBAL`` carries the module and name in
its argument; ``STACK_GLOBAL`` (protocol 4 and later) takes them from the two
strings pushed just before it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pickletools

from modelgate.policy import PICKLE_BLOCKLIST, SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS
from modelgate.report import Finding

_STRING_OPS = {"SHORT_BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE", "BINUNICODE8", "UNICODE", "STRING", "SHORT_BINSTRING", "BINSTRING"}
_MEMO_PUT_OPS = {"MEMOIZE", "BINPUT", "LONG_BINPUT", "PUT"}  # the pickler memoizes every string it writes


def scan_pickle(data: bytes, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    recent: list[str] = []  # the last two string pushes, for STACK_GLOBAL
    try:
        for op, arg, pos in pickletools.genops(data):
            if op.name in _STRING_OPS:
                recent = (recent + [str(arg)])[-2:]
                for needle in SUSPICIOUS_STRINGS:
                    if needle in str(arg):
                        findings.append(Finding("code-execution", f"{location}@{pos}", f"suspicious string {needle!r} in data"))
                        break
                continue
            if op.name == "GLOBAL":
                module, name = str(arg).split(" ", 1)
                _check_global(module, name, f"{location}@{pos}", findings)

import pickletools, sys, io
def dis_stream(data, maxlines=400):

        out=io.StringIO()

data=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read()

arguments.content:
"""Knowledge base: which callables carry a capability of the policy.

Keys are canonical names, ``<module>.<qualname>`` of the object the name
resolves to, with module aliases normalised (``posix``/``nt`` -> ``os``,
``_io`` -> ``io``, ``_socket`` -> ``socket`` ...; see ``MODULE_ALIASES``).
Methods are keyed by ``<module>.<Class>.<method>`` and receive ``self`` as
their first argument.  A value is ``(kind, condition)``; ``condition`` is
``None`` (always) or a function ``(args, kwargs) -> bool`` deciding whether
the call reaches the capability.

The tables cover the policy's seed list and the other standard-library and
common third-party callables with the same capabilities.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

CODE = "code-execution"
PROC = "process"
FILE = "file-access"
NET = "network"

# module name normalisation applied to canonical names and to imports
MODULE_ALIASES = {
    "posix": "os",
    "nt": "os",
    "posixpath": "os.path",
    "ntpath": "os.path",
    "_io": "io",
    "_pyio": "io",
    "_pickle": "pickle",
    "_socket": "socket",
    "_operator": "operator",
    "_functools": "functools",
    "_collections": "collections",
    "_collections_abc": "collections.abc",
    "_codecs": "codecs",
    "_ssl": "ssl",
    "_sqlite3": "sqlite3",
    "_ctypes": "ctypes",
    "_json": "json",
    "_heapq": "heapq",
    "_bisect": "bisect",
    "_struct": "struct",
    "_random": "random",
    "_datetime": "datetime",
    "_weakref": "weakref",
    "_signal": "signal",
    "_locale": "locale",
    "_string": "string",
    "_bz2": "bz2",
    "_lzma": "lzma",
    "_thread": "_thread",
    "_asyncio": "asyncio",
    "_compression": "_compression",
}

# Modules whose names, when they appear as an attribute of a module the
# scanner does not import (``torch.os``), are taken to be that module.
COMMON_MODULE_ATTRS = {
    "os", "sys", "subprocess", "shutil", "socket", "builtins", "pickle", "io",
    "importlib", "pathlib", "tempfile", "marshal", "types", "functools",
    "operator", "runpy", "code", "pty", "platform", "ctypes", "urllib",
    "http", "ftplib", "smtplib", "webbrowser", "codecs", "base64", "zlib",
    "json", "logging", "threading", "multiprocessing", "collections",
    "itertools", "inspect", "warnings", "glob", "copy", "copyreg", "pydoc",
    "timeit", "pdb", "bdb", "posix", "nt", "signal", "asyncio", "ssl",
}


def _arg(args, kwargs, idx, name, default=None):
    if len(args) > idx:
        return args[idx]
    return kwargs.get(name, default)


def _truthy_arg(idx, name, default=None):
    def cond(args, kwargs):
        v = _arg(args, kwargs, idx, name, default)
        if isinstance(v, (str, bytes)) or v is None:
            return bool(v)
        return True  # symbolic: assume a host was given
    return cond


def _not_none_arg(idx, name):
    def cond(args, kwargs):
        return _arg(args, kwargs, idx, name, None) is not None
    return cond


def _path_arg(idx, name):
    """A path-like argument (not a file object / in-memory buffer)."""
    from modelgate.symbolic import FileObj

    def cond(args, kwargs):
        v = _arg(args, kwargs, idx, name, None)
        if v is None:
            return False
        if isinstance(v, FileObj) and v.path is None:
            return False
        return True
    return cond


def _sqlite_path(args, kwargs):
    v = _arg(args, kwargs, 0, "database", None)
    if isinstance(v, str) and (v == ":memory:" or v.startswith("file::memory:") or v == ""):
        return False
    if isinstance(v, bytes) and v in (b":memory:", b""):
        return False
    return True


def _not_delay(args, kwargs):
    # logging.FileHandler(filename, mode='a', encoding=None, delay=False, errors=None)
    v = _arg(args, kwargs, 3, "delay", False)
    return not (v is True or v == 1)


def _not_delay_rot(idx):
    def cond(args, kwargs):
        v = _arg(args, kwargs, idx, "delay", False)
        return not (v is True or v == 1)
    return cond


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# functions and methods: calling them performs the capability
CAPS: dict[str, tuple] = {}

"""Knowledge base: which callables carry a capability of the policy.

Keys are canonical names, ``<module>.<qualname>`` of the object the name
resolves to, with module aliases normalised (``posix``/``nt`` -> ``os``,
``_io`` -> ``io``, ``_socket`` -> ``socket`` ...; see ``MODULE_ALIASES``).
Methods are keyed by ``<module>.<Class>.<method>`` and receive ``self`` as
their first argument.  A value is ``(kind, condition)``; ``condition`` is
``None`` (always) or a function ``(args, kwargs) -> bool`` deciding whether
the call reaches the capability.

The tables cover the policy's seed list and the other standard-library and
common third-party callables with the same capabilities.
"""

# scanner does not import (``torch.os``), are taken to be that module.

def _arg(args, kwargs, idx, name, default=None):
    if len(args) > idx:
        return args[idx]
    return kwargs.get(name, default)


def _truthy_arg(idx, name, default=None):
    def cond(args, kwargs):
        v = _arg(args, kwargs, idx, name, default)
        if isinstance(v, (str, bytes)) or v is None:
            return bool(v)
        return True  # symbolic: assume a host was given
    return cond


def _not_none_arg(idx, name):
    def cond(args, kwargs):
        return _arg(args, kwargs, idx, name, None) is not None
    return cond


def _path_arg(idx, name):
    """A path-like argument (not a file object / in-memory buffer)."""
    from modelgate.symbolic import FileObj

    def cond(args, kwargs):
        v = _arg(args, kwargs, idx, name, None)
        if v is None:
            return False
        if isinstance(v, FileObj) and v.path is None:
            return False
        return True
    return cond


def _sqlite_path(args, kwargs):
    v = _arg(args, kwargs, 0, "database", None)
    if isinstance(v, str) and (v == ":memory:" or v.startswith("file::memory:") or v == ""):
        return False
    if isinstance(v, bytes) and v in (b":memory:", b""):

    return True

    # logging.FileHandler(filename, mode='a', encoding=None, delay=False, errors=None)
    v = _arg(args, kwargs, 3, "delay", False)
    return not (v is True or v == 1)

    def cond(args, kwargs):
        v = _arg(args, kwargs, idx, "delay", False)
        return not (v is True or v == 1)
    return cond

Methods are keyed by ``<module>.<Class>.<method>`` and receive ``self`` as
their first argument.  A value is ``(kind, condition)``; ``condition`` is

the call reaches the capability.

arguments.content:
"""TensorFlow SavedModel: the policy's closed op table.

Every ``meta_graphs[*]`` is in scope and, within each, ``graph_def.node`` and
every ``graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`` (which covers functions
referenced through ``If``/``While``/``PartitionedCall``... attributes).  Only
the ``op`` of a node carries a capability; names, devices, attributes and
tensor contents are data.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re

OP_KINDS = {}
for _op in "PyFunc PyFuncStateless EagerPyFunc".split():
    OP_KINDS[_op] = "code-execution"
for _op in """ReadFile WriteFile MatchingFiles MatchingFilesDataset ImmutableConst WholeFileReader
        WholeFileReaderV2 TextLineReader TextLineReaderV2 FixedLengthRecordReader
        FixedLengthRecordReaderV2 TFRecordReader TFRecordReaderV2 LMDBReader LMDBDataset
        ExperimentalLMDBDataset TextLineDataset TFRecordDataset FixedLengthRecordDataset
        DatasetToTFRecord ExperimentalDatasetToTFRecord SaveDataset SaveDatasetV2 LoadDataset
        SnapshotDataset SnapshotDatasetV2 LoadAndRemapMatrix GenerateVocabRemapping Save
        SaveSlices Restore RestoreSlice""".split():
    OP_KINDS[_op] = "file-access"
for _op in """DataServiceDataset DataServiceDatasetV2 DataServiceDatasetV3 DataServiceDatasetV4
        RegisterDataset RegisterDatasetV2 DistributedSave""".split():
    OP_KINDS[_op] = "network"


def _check_graph(I, mg, mi, location):
    gd = mg.graph_def
    for node in gd.node:
        kind = OP_KINDS.get(node.op)
        if kind:
            I.finding(kind, f"op {node.op}", f"{location}:meta_graphs[{mi}].graph_def.node[{node.name}]")
    for fn in gd.library.function:
        fname = fn.signature.name
        for node in fn.node_def:
            kind = OP_KINDS.get(node.op)
            if kind:
                I.finding(kind, f"op {node.op}",
                          f"{location}:meta_graphs[{mi}].library.function[{fname}].node[{node.name}]")


_OP_RE = re.compile(r'(?m)^\s*op\s*:\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"')


def scan_proto_bytes(I, data: bytes, location: str, text: bool = False):
    try:
        from modelgate.tfproto import saved_model_pb2
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        I.finding("unsupported", f"cannot load protobuf bindings: {exc}", location)
        return
    sm = saved_model_pb2.SavedModel()
    try:
        if text:
            from google.protobuf import text_format

            text_format.Parse(data.decode("utf-8"), sm, allow_unknown_extension=True,
                              allow_unknown_field=True)
        else:
            sm.ParseFromString(data)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        if text:
            # fall back to the node ops written in the text proto
            try:
                body = data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                body = ""
            for m in _OP_RE.finditer(body):
                kind = OP_KINDS.get(m.group(1))
                if kind:
                    I.finding(kind, f"op {m.group(1)}", f"{location}:offset {m.start()}")
            return
        I.finding("unsupported", f"cannot parse SavedModel protobuf: {type(exc).__name__}", location)
        return
    for mi, mg in enumerate(sm.meta_graphs):
        _check_graph(I, mg, mi, location)


def scan_saved_model_dir(I, path: str, location: str) -> bool:
    """Scan a SavedModel directory; False if it is not one."""
    pb = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pb")
    pbtxt = os.path.join(path, "saved_model.pbtxt")
    if os.path.isfile(pb):
        with open(pb, "rb") as fh:

"""Keras HDF5 scanning: Lambda layers in the model configuration."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

from modelgate.report import Finding


def scan_h5(path: str, location: str) -> list[Finding]:
    import h5py  # lazy: only needed for Keras files

    with h5py.File(path, "r") as fh:
        raw = fh.attrs.get("model_config")
    if raw is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(raw, bytes):
        raw = raw.decode("utf-8")
    config = json.loads(raw)
    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for i, layer in enumerate(config.get("config", {}).get("layers", [])):
        if layer.get("class_name") == "Lambda":
            findings.append(Finding("code-execution", f"{location}:layers[{i}]", "Lambda layer"))
    return findings

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ModelGate command line.

    python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output <report.json> <path> [<path> ...]

Writes one JSON report (see /app/docs/report-schema.md) and exits 0 once it
is written; exits 2 on a usage error.  ``-I`` keeps the script directory off
sys.path, so the package directory's parent is added explicitly below.

The scan never runs anything from the artifact and writes no file other
than the report (bytecode caching is disabled before anything is imported).
"""
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True

import argparse  # noqa: E402
import os  # noqa: E402
import signal  # noqa: E402
import time  # noqa: E402
import warnings  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

TIME_BUDGET = 48.0  # seconds for all paths of one invocation (registry limit: 60)


class _Timeout(Exception):
    pass


def _on_alarm(signum, frame):  # pragma: no cover - only on pathological input
    raise _Timeout()


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="modelgate", description="static scanner for model artifacts")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version="modelgate")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    scan = sub.add_parser("scan", help="scan one or more artifacts")
    scan.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="where to write the JSON report")
    scan.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="artifact files, or SavedModel directories")
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        return 2 if exc.code else 0

    from modelgate import __version__  # noqa: F401
    from modelgate.report import Finding, Result, to_json

    started = time.monotonic()
    results = []
    sys.setrecursionlimit(max(sys.getrecursionlimit(), 12000))
    try:
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _on_alarm)
    except (ValueError, AttributeError, OSError):
        pass
    for i, path in enumerate(args.paths):
        remaining = TIME_BUDGET - (time.monotonic() - started)
        share = max(1.0, remaining / max(1, len(args.paths) - i))
        deadline = time.monotonic() + share * 0.9

def sm(nodes=(), funcs=(), metas=None, tensor_str=None):
    s = saved_model_pb2.SavedModel()
    s.saved_model_schema_version = 1
    for mi, (mnodes, mfuncs) in enumerate(metas or [(nodes, funcs)]):
        mg = s.meta_graphs.add()
        mg.meta_info_def.tags.append("serve" if mi == 0 else "train")
        for nname, op in mnodes:
            n = mg.graph_def.node.add()
            n.name = nname
            n.op = op
            if tensor_str:

                n.attr["note"].s = tensor_str.encode()
        for fname, fnodes in mfuncs:
            f = mg.graph_def.library.function.add()
            f.signature.name = fname
            for nname, op in fnodes:
                n = f.node_def.add()
                n.name = nname
                n.op = op
    return s

    open(os.path.join(d, "variables", "variables.index"), "wb").write(b"\x00" * 16)

def joblib_array_pickle(arr_bytes_count=4, payload=b""):
    dtype = call(g("numpy", "dtype"), u("f8"), FALSE, TRUE) + tup(i(3), u("<"), NONE, NONE, NONE, b"J\xff\xff\xff\xff", b"J\xff\xff\xff\xff", i(0)) + BUILD

             u("order") + u("C") + u("dtype") + dtype + u("allow_mmap") + TRUE +

"""Mutation fuzzing of the emulator: no unexpected exceptions allowed."""
import os, sys, random, glob, time, traceback
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
sys.path.insert(0, "/app")
from modelgate import formats
from modelgate.interp import Interp
from modelgate.symbolic import Exhausted

seeds = []
for d in ("/tmp/work/cases", "/tmp/work/cases2", "/app/samples"):
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(d + "/*")):
        if os.path.isfile(f) and not f.endswith(".json"):
            seeds.append(open(f, "rb").read())
rng = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 0)
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3000
ops = list(b"().0123NIJKLMFSTUVXabcdeghijlopqrstu}])\x80\x81\x82\x85\x86\x87\x88\x89\x8a\x8c\x8f\x90\x91\x92\x93\x94\x95\x96\x97\x98QRPB")
errs = {}
t0 = time.time()
for n in range(N):
    data = bytearray(rng.choice(seeds))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)):
        k = rng.random()
        if not data:
            break
        i = rng.randrange(len(data))
        if k < 0.3:
            data[i] = rng.choice(ops)
        elif k < 0.5:
            data[i] = rng.randrange(256)
        elif k < 0.7:
            del data[i:i + rng.randint(1, 8)]
        elif k < 0.85:
            other = rng.choice(seeds)
            j = rng.randrange(len(other))
            data[i:i] = other[j:j + rng.randint(1, 40)]
        else:
            data[i:i] = bytes([rng.choice(ops)]) * rng.randint(1, 4)
    I = Interp(deadline=time.monotonic() + 10)
    try:
        formats.analyze_blob(I, bytes(data), "fuzz")
    except Exhausted:
        pass
    except Exception as exc:
        key = f"ESCAPED {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:150]
        errs.setdefault(key, (bytes(data), traceback.format_exc()))
    for e in I.internal_errors:
        key = e.split(": ", 1)[1][:150] if ": " in e else e
        errs.setdefault(key, (bytes(data), e))
print(f"{N} runs in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s; distinct errors: {len(errs)}")
for k, (d, tb) in list(errs.items())[:25]:
    print("----", k)
    print(tb[-1500:] if "Traceback" in tb else tb)
EOF

        "start", "run", "upper", "path", "__call__", "check_output", "get", "x", "", "builtins", "eval", "1"]


def gen(rng, nops=None):
    proto_n = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
    out = [proto(proto_n) if proto_n >= 2 else b""]
    depth = 0  # rough stack depth tracking
    marks = 0
    nops = nops or rng.randint(3, 30)
    memo_n = 0
    for _ in range(nops):
        r = rng.random()
        if r < 0.18:
            m, n = rng.choice(GLOBALS)
            out.append(g(m, n) if rng.random() < 0.5 or proto_n < 4 else sg(m, n)); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.22:
            m, n = rng.choice(DOTTED)
            out.append(g(m, n) if rng.random() < 0.5 else sg(m, n)); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.35:
            out.append(u(rng.choice(STRS))); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.38:
            out.append(i(rng.randint(0, 3))); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.40:
            out.append(NONE); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.47:
            out.append(MARK); marks += 1
        elif r < 0.55 and marks:
            out.append(TUPLE); marks -= 1; depth += 1
        elif r < 0.58 and marks:
            out.append(LIST); marks -= 1; depth += 1
        elif r < 0.60:
            out.append(EMPTY_TUPLE); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.62 and depth >= 1:
            out.append(TUPLE1)
        elif r < 0.64 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(TUPLE2); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.75 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(REDUCE); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.78 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(BUILD); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.80 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(NEWOBJ); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.84 and depth >= 1:
            out.append(put(memo_n % 256)); memo_n += 1
        elif r < 0.87 and memo_n:
            out.append(get(rng.randrange(min(memo_n, 256)))); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.89 and depth >= 1:
            out.append(POP); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.91:
            out.append(EMPTY_LIST); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.93:
            out.append(EMPTY_DICT); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.95 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(APPEND); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.97 and depth >= 3:
            out.append(SETITEM); depth -= 2
        elif marks and depth >= 1:
            out.append(b"o"); marks -= 1
        else:
            out.append(DUP); depth += 1
    out.append(STOP)
    data = b"".join(out)
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        data += gen(rng, rng.randint(3, 10))
    return data

    seed = int(sys.argv[1]); n = int(sys.argv[2]); outd = sys.argv[3]

    json.dump(exp, open(os.path.join(outd, "expected.json"), "w"))

def gen(rng, nops=None):
    proto_n = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5])

    depth = 0  # rough stack depth tracking
    marks = 0

        elif r < 0.38:
            out.append(i(rng.randint(0, 3))); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.40:
            out.append(NONE); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.47:
            out.append(MARK); marks += 1
        elif r < 0.55 and marks:
            out.append(TUPLE); marks -= 1; depth += 1
        elif r < 0.58 and marks:
            out.append(LIST); marks -= 1; depth += 1
        elif r < 0.60:
            out.append(EMPTY_TUPLE); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.62 and depth >= 1:
            out.append(TUPLE1)
        elif r < 0.64 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(TUPLE2); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.75 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(REDUCE); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.78 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(BUILD); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.80 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(NEWOBJ); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.84 and depth >= 1:
            out.append(put(memo_n % 256)); memo_n += 1
        elif r < 0.87 and memo_n:
            out.append(get(rng.randrange(min(memo_n, 256)))); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.89 and depth >= 1:
            out.append(POP); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.91:
            out.append(EMPTY_LIST); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.93:
            out.append(EMPTY_DICT); depth += 1
        elif r < 0.95 and depth >= 2:
            out.append(APPEND); depth -= 1
        elif r < 0.97 and depth >= 3:
            out.append(SETITEM); depth -= 2
        elif marks and depth >= 1:
            out.append(b"o"); marks -= 1
        else:
            out.append(DUP); depth += 1
    out.append(STOP)
    data = b"".join(out)
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        data += gen(rng, rng.randint(3, 10))

steps.reasoning_content: Review found that `bytearray.__new__` makes an empty bytearray, `weakref.finalize` registers in `__init__` so NEWOBJ registers nothing, and `type.__new__` does build a class. I'm fixing the `__new__`-only table now.

arguments.command:
cd /app/modelgate && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='handlers.py'; s=open(p).read()
old='''@h("weakref.finalize", new=True)
def _finalize(I, f, args, kwargs):'''
new='''@h("weakref.finalize")
def _finalize(I, f, args, kwargs):'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
s += '''

# bytearray.__new__ makes an empty array (the content is set by __init__)
NEW_HANDLERS["builtins.bytearray"] = lambda I, f, args, kwargs: bytearray()
# type.__new__(type, name, bases, ns) builds a class
NEW_HANDLERS["builtins.type"] = lambda I, f, args, kwargs: _type(I, f, args, kwargs) if len(args) == 3 \\
    else Inst(f, args, kwargs, False)
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "new=True" handlers.py | head -40

def resolve(name):
    parts = name.split('.')
    for k in range(len(parts)-1, 0, -1):
        try: m = importlib.import_module('.'.join(parts[:k]))
        except Exception: continue
        o = m
        try:
            for p in parts[k:]: o = getattr(o, p)
            return o
        except AttributeError: continue

for d in dead: print(*d)

        try:

        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - e.g. sum() of bytes raises TypeError

    return Opaque("sum")'''

arguments.command:

        return Opaque("bytes")'''
new='''        if all(isinstance(x, int) for x in items):
            try:
                return f.obj(items)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                raise LoadError("bytes() failed") from None
        if any(is_plain(x) and not isinstance(x, int) for x in items):

steps.reasoning_content: While the run continues, I'm making my SIGALRM timeout and step/time-budget exceptions derive from BaseException instead of Exception, so a broad `except Exception` can't swallow them and let a slow scan overrun to the hard watchdog.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='/app/modelgate/symbolic.py'; s=open(p).read()
old='''class Exhausted(Exception):
    """The analysis budget for one artifact is spent."""'''
new='''class Exhausted(BaseException):
    """The analysis budget for one artifact is spent (a BaseException so that
    no ``except Exception`` on the way swallows it)."""'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s)
p='/app/modelgate/cli.py'; s=open(p).read()
old='''class _Timeout(Exception):
    pass'''
new='''class _Timeout(BaseException):
    """Raised by SIGALRM; not an Exception, so nothing swallows it."""'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -rn "except Exhausted\|Exhausted)" /app/modelgate/*.py | head

def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="modelgate", description="static scanner for model artifacts")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version="modelgate")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    scan = sub.add_parser("scan", help="scan one or more artifacts")
    scan.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="where to write the JSON report")
    scan.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="artifact files, or SavedModel directories")
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        return 2 if exc.code else 0

    from modelgate import __version__  # noqa: F401
    from modelgate.report import Finding, Result, to_json

    started = time.monotonic()
    results = []

    def write(final_results):
        with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape") as fh:
            fh.write(to_json(final_results))

    def provisional(done):
        # fail-closed placeholder for the paths not scanned yet, so that a
        # report exists even if a native library never returns
        pending = [Result(p, [Finding("unsupported", p, "scan did not complete")])
                   for p in args.paths[len(done):]]
        write(done + pending)

    provisional([])
    try:
        import faulthandler

        faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(HARD_LIMIT, exit=True)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        faulthandler = None
    sys.setrecursionlimit(max(sys.getrecursionlimit(), 12000))
    try:
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _on_alarm)
    except (ValueError, AttributeError, OSError):
        pass
    for i, path in enumerate(args.paths):
        remaining = TIME_BUDGET - (time.monotonic() - started)
        share = max(1.0, remaining / max(1, len(args.paths) - i))
        deadline = time.monotonic() + share * 0.9
        try:
            signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, share)
        except (ValueError, AttributeError, OSError):
            pass
        try:
            from modelgate import dispatch

            results.append(dispatch.scan_path(path, deadline=deadline))
        except _Timeout:
            results.append(Result(path, [Finding("unsupported", path, "scan did not finish within the time limit")]))
        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a crash must still yield a verdict
            if isinstance(exc, KeyboardInterrupt):
                raise
            msg = f"scanner error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:300].encode("utf-8", "backslashreplace").decode()
            results.append(Result(path, [Finding("unsupported", path, msg)]))
        finally:
            try:
                signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
            except (ValueError, AttributeError, OSError):
                pass
        if i + 1 < len(args.paths):
            provisional(results)
    write(results)

arguments.content:
# ModelGate internals

`python3 -I /app/modelgate/cli.py scan --output report.json <path>`; the report
contract is `/app/docs/report-schema.md`, the policy `/app/docs/threat-model.md`.

## How a verdict is reached

1. **Format by content** (`formats.analyze_blob`, `containers.sniff`): gzip
   (all members), bz2, xz, zlib, lzma-alone, zip (central directory decides,
   last same-name entry wins, bytes before the archive tolerated), tar, `.npy`,
   HDF5, otherwise pickle stream(s). Containers recurse (depth limit 8).
   A zip with `<prefix>/data.pkl` and a local header at offset 0 is a torch
   checkpoint (only `data.pkl` is unpickled, with torch's persistent ids); a zip
   with `config.json` + `metadata.json`/`model.weights.h5` is a `.keras` archive;
   a zip of `.npy` members is an `.npz`; any other zip/tar is an archive whose
   members are loaded by their own content. A directory (or archive directory)
   with `saved_model.pb`/`.pbtxt` is a SavedModel (`.pb` wins).
2. **Pickles** are executed by `pickle_vm.Machine`, a re-implementation of the
   C unpickler (marks/fences, memo, `PROTO`-dependent `find_class` incl.
   `fix_imports` and dotted names, `PERSID`, framing, error behaviour), over
   symbolic values. Raw files: `pickle.load` until EOF; legacy torch files
   (first pickle = magic): exactly five pickles. Where the real loader raises,
   the stream stops — nothing after it runs.
3. **Calls** go through `interp.Interp`: globals resolve to real objects of
   side-effect-free standard-library modules (never anything from the
   artifact; third-party modules are symbolic), BUILD/`setattr`/`vars()`
   rebinding, `sys.modules`, getattr/attrgetter/methodcaller/partial/map/
   reduce/threads/executors ... are modelled in `handlers.py`; a call that
   reaches a callable listed in `kb.CAPS` (after the argument checks that make
   the real call raise first) is a finding. Nested loaders (`nested.py`) are
   judged by what they would load, after decoding/assembly of the embedded data.
4. **Keras**: Lambda `function`/`output_shape` bytecode and `activation`
   `__lambda__` dicts, anywhere layers nest (`keras_scan`, `h5lite`).
   **TensorFlow**: the closed op table over every meta graph, graph node and
   library function node (`savedmodel_scan`).

## Deliberate judgement calls

* Unknown top-level modules that are neither standard library nor a known
  ML/data package (`kb.KNOWN_THIRD_PARTY`) fail to import, as they would.
* Modules in `sys.modules` lookups are assumed loaded; `nt` is `os` (policy).
* `logging.config.dictConfig`, `timeit.*`, `compile` are findings whenever
  called (seed list: they evaluate/compile source).
* Directory listing / `stat` / `exists` are not file access; `open` for
  reading is.
* Fail closed (`unsupported`) only when the scan cannot finish (time budget,
  nesting) or the emulator itself failed and nothing else was found.

## Safety of the scanner itself

No subprocesses, no network, no writes except the report (bytecode caching is
off). Real functions are only evaluated for an allowlist of pure helpers on
plain data with size guards (`interp.PURE*`, `size_ok`). HDF5 attributes are
read by the bounded `h5lite` parser; libhdf5 is only used for layouts it does
not handle. A provisional fail-closed report is written first and a C-level
watchdog (`faulthandler`) ends the process before the 60 s limit if a native
call never returns.

## Extending

Add capability callables to `kb.CAPS` by canonical name (`module.qualname`
with module aliases normalised, see `interp.canonical`); add call semantics
(callers, indirection) to `handlers.py` with `@h("canonical.name")`.

steps.message:
I've rebuilt ModelGate so its verdicts follow the threat model. On the 30 samples it now catches 15 of 15 malicious artifacts with no false positives (it was 6/15 caught and 3 clean ones flagged). The command line and report format are unchanged, and it scans about 0.1–0.2 s per artifact, so a 560-artifact pass takes roughly 75 s.

**What it does now**
- **Pickles:** instead of matching names, the scanner replays the file the way Python's real unpickler would, without running anything. It decides by what actually gets called. A global or a dangerous-looking string stored as data is clean. A call is malicious however it's reached: through the memo, `getattr` chains, `partial` retargeting, a module rebound by BUILD, `sys.modules`, `pkgutil.resolve_name`, `map`/`sorted`/`reduce`, threads and executors, or a second pickle stream. Calls that fail before acting stop the load, so anything after them doesn't count (non-tuple REDUCE arguments, dotted names below protocol 4, Python 2 module names at protocol 3+, `PERSID` in a plain pickle). Embedded pickles passed to another loader are decoded first (base64, zlib, hex, concatenation, bytearrays) and judged by what they load.
- **Formats and containers:** the format is decided from content, not extension: PyTorch zip and legacy checkpoints, `.npy`/`.npz`, joblib (including inline arrays), and gz/bz2/xz/zip/tar nested to any reasonable depth. For zips, the central directory decides and the last entry with a name wins.
- **TensorFlow:** the exact op table from the policy (checked mechanically, 42 ops), applied to every meta-graph, every graph node and every library function.
- **Keras:** bytecode in a Lambda's `function`/`output_shape` and `__lambda__` activations, wherever layers are nested.

**How I checked it.** The emulator was compared against the real unpickler, run in a separate process under an audit hook that records and blocks process, file, network and exec events. That comparison covered about 18,000 hand-written and randomly generated pickles. The few disagreements were all reviewed:
- noise from the checking harness itself;
- calls whose outcome depends on the loading process (`vars()` with no argument, `SMTP()` resolving the local host name);
- two edge cases I can't decide statically (whether an `ssl` socket is wrapped with a hostname, the length of an iterator).

Formats with no runnable loader here (torch, Keras, TensorFlow, archives) were covered by 110 hand-labelled cases. Every callable in the policy's seed list was tested through several routes and containers (567 variants, all caught). Fuzzing with 40,000 mutated files produced no crashes. I confirmed that a scan writes nothing except the report.

**Judgment calls the hidden corpus could disagree with:**
- A module that is neither standard library nor a known ML/data package counts as not installed, so loading stops there.
- A zip with `<prefix>/data.pkl` and a header at offset 0 is a torch checkpoint, so only `data.pkl` is loaded and any extra pickle members are ignored.
- `.npz` members are treated as loaded.
- `dictConfig`, `timeit` and `compile` are flagged whenever they are called.
- `platform.platform()` is flagged, because it really does start `uname -p`.
- Directory listings and `stat` calls are not treated as file access.
- When the scan can't finish within about 48 s, the verdict is `unsupported`, as the contract requires.

**Safety.** The scanner never imports anything an artifact names except side-effect-free standard-library modules, and no pickle ever runs. It writes a fail-closed report first, then overwrites it at the end. A native watchdog stops the process before the 60 s limit if a native library call hangs. In that case the fail-closed report stays, but the exit status is 1, not 0. HDF5 headers are parsed with a small bounded reader of my own, because libhdf5 hung forever on some corrupted files during fuzzing.

The code is in `/app/modelgate/`; `README.md` there explains the design and how to add new dangerous callables.
